phase: Phase 1: Page B in the preview folder (by Wed 2026-11-18)
summary: Round 5 passes. Each round 4 finding is fixed, and a test that fails on 46002d0 pins each fix (9 failed, 76 passed). No earlier round regressed. One Minor item and two Nits remain. The Minor item is an unreadable directory under docs: preview.sh exits 1 with a find message, not the stated refusal line. No docs write is possible.
nonblocking_findings: A5-1 [Minor] review-a: harness/model-guide/preview.sh:105-110 (symlink scan) with the header at preview.sh:11-14 and the comment at preview.sh:113-115: The claim that preview.sh refuses an unreadable entry under docs (mode 000 file or folder) with `preview: unreadable <path>` and exit 2 holds only for a file. An unreadable directory makes the symlink scan `LINK="$(find "$ROOT/docs" -type l -print -quit)"` fail: find prints `find: <path>: Permission denied` on stderr and exits 1, and `set -e` ends the script. Probes in git archive copies of 0acceea: docs/e mode 000 (empty), docs/a/b mode 000 (nested), and docs/e mode 311 each gave exit 1, empty stdout, one find line on stderr, and no preview folder and no .tmp folder. A mode 000 file gave exit 2 and `preview: unreadable docs/locked.txt`. No file is written, so the failure is safe. It is the same family as round 4 A4-1 and A4-3, at a new place. The two A4-1 tests use a file only, so nothing pins the directory case. Fix: run the unreadable scan before the symlink scan, or give the symlink scan `2>/dev/null || true`; add a preview test with an unreadable directory that expects exit 2, `preview: unreadable docs/<dir>`, and empty stderr; or narrow the header and the comment to files.

A5-2 [Nit] review-a: harness/model-guide/preview.sh:105-122 and the python step at preview.sh:140-160: preview.sh refuses symlinks and unreadable entries but not other special files under docs. With a FIFO at docs/f.pipe in a temp copy, preview.sh did not end in 25 s: `cp -a` copied the FIFO, then the python `sha256_file` opened it and blocked. The preview folder was left half built (it existed after the timeout). publish.ts maps the same entry to `publish: drift f.pipe` through the lstat walk (isFile false). Git cannot track a FIFO, so the tracked docs tree cannot hold one, and no docs write is possible. Fix: add `find "$ROOT/docs" ! -type f ! -type d -print -quit` to the shell scans and refuse with `preview: refused path <path>`.

A5-3 [Nit] review-a: harness/model-guide-tests/preview-gate.test.ts:1128-1136 (test B2-1 preview dangling): The dangling-link case now gives `preview: refused path <abs link>` (probe: exit 2, empty stderr, no folder). The B2-1 test asserts only exit 2, no traceback, and an unchanged docs snapshot. The three B3-1 preview tests cover a relative link, an outside link, and a directory link, with exact lines, but no test pins the line for a dangling link. A change of that line would pass. Fix: assert `preview: refused path <abs link>\n` in the B2-1 test.

B3-1 fixed in publish.ts: publish.ts:99-121 walks docs with lstatSync, and a symlink or any non-file entry goes to the broken list (publish.ts:119-120), which becomes `publish: drift <path>` before the copy loop at publish.ts:169-173. Probes in temp copies: a relative link planted after the preview gave exit 2, `publish: drift alias.html`, docs unchanged; a directory link with an approved row beneath it gave exit 2, `publish: drift dl`, and the outside folder stayed empty; a mode 000 file gave exit 2, `publish: drift l.txt`; the control publish gave exit 0 and wrote only docs/real-work.html and docs/real-work.json. The three B3-1 publish tests fail on 46002d0 (two write through the link with exit 0, one names `dirlink/secret.txt`) and pass at 0acceea. They build the preview base by hand (writeDocsBase), so they pin publish.ts without preview.sh.

A4-3 fixed: publish.ts:101-107 wraps readdirSync and pushes the directory path to the broken list. Probe: a nested mode 000 directory docs/a/b gave exit 2, `publish: drift a/b`, empty stderr, and no real-work file in docs (0 matches). The A4-3 test failed on 46002d0 (EACCES stack, exit 1) and passes at 0acceea.
